summary: Researched and prototyped the spec->Revit-editable generation paths. IfcOpenShell 0.8.5 installs cleanly as a native mac-arm64/py3.12 wheel; experiments/gen_ifc_min.py now emits a validated IFC4 house (project/site/building, 2 storeys, 4 walls, 2 slabs, door+window voiding host walls) verified by EXPRESS-rule validation and OpenCascade tessellation (wall volumes drop by exactly the opening volume). Documented Revit's real IFC-import fidelity (Link = category-mapped DirectShapes, IFC4; Open = legacy IFC2x3 nativisation attempt) with sources, dissected APS Automation for Revit (with Autodesk's own SketchIt JSON->rvt sample vendored as the reference architecture), ODA BimRv (writes latest .rvt from a template; Sustaining membership US$7.5k/4.5k + module), and Speckle/Hypar/pyRevit/gbXML alternatives. Designed the versioned parameterized building spec (spec/building.schema.json, JSON Schema 2020-12) where everything but a footprint is defaultable, with tiny/house/office examples that validate. Recommendation: one spec compiler front-end with two back-ends — IFC (ship now, free, local, also the regression oracle) then a C# IExternalDBApplication on APS Automation as the primary native-.rvt path; ODA BimRv as contingency only.
key_findings: `uv pip install ifcopenshell` installs ifcopenshell==0.8.5 as a prebuilt mac-arm64 CPython-3.12 wheel (pulls numpy 2.5, shapely 2.1) with the OpenCascade kernel included; no source build or conda needed. Also installed pytest (required by ifcopenshell.validate express-rule executor, which imports _pytest) and jsonschema.

experiments/gen_ifc_min.py emits experiments/out/min_house.ifc: 342 entities, IFC4, IfcProject>Site>Building>2 storeys, 4 IfcWall (STANDARD, 8x6 m room, 6 m tall), 2 IfcSlab, IfcDoor+IfcWindow each filling an IfcOpeningElement that voids its host wall; reopens, passes schema + EXPRESS-rule validation with 0 errors, and OCC tessellation confirms voids applied (Wall-0 9.222 m3 = 9.6 - door 0.378; Wall-2 9.240 = 9.6 - window 0.36; slabs 12.0 m3). Build time 0.12 s. The script also validates the four spec examples against the schema (all OK).

Two IfcOpenShell 0.8.5 gotchas: geometry.create_2pt_wall returns the body representation and sets placement but does NOT assign it (walls are geometry-less unless you call assign_representation); validate(express_rules=True) needs pytest installed.

Revit IFC import: Link IFC (recommended, supports IFC4) runs the open-source revit-ifc importer producing a cached .ifc.RVT of DirectShapes with correct category from the IFC-class mapping and IFC props as shared parameters -- viewable/taggable/schedulable but NOT parametric or host-able (2024+ 'hybrid' AnyCAD import improves solids but the object model is unchanged). Open IFC is the legacy importer scoped by Autodesk's own help to IFC2x3/2x2/2x (link adds IFC4); it can nativise simple IfcWallStandardCase extrusions into Basic Walls and puts doors/windows in as in-place families, with inconsistent results. Therefore an IFC-based path can never yield fully native host-able elements; the generator should emit both IFC4 (for Link) and an IFC2X3 IfcWallStandardCase flavour (for Open), controlled by spec targets.ifc.

APS Automation (Design Automation) for Revit is the sanctioned headless native path: revitcoreconsole runs a DB-only add-in (IExternalDBApplication + DesignAutomationBridge ready event) via AppBundle/Activity/WorkItem with OSS signed-URL I/O and 2-legged OAuth. Autodesk's own SketchIt sample (vendored at vendor/sketchit) is literally 'JSON walls+floors -> new .rvt' in ~150 LOC using rvtApp.NewProjectDocument, Wall.Create, doc.Create.NewFloor, SaveAs -- our exact architecture. Pricing moved 2025-12-08 to a free/paid metered model (processing-hour rated, Flex tokens; exact current Revit-engine rate must be re-verified).

ODA BimRv SDK writes .rvt without Autodesk software: reads 2011+, writes latest-version-only with full/incremental save, but creation requires a template .rvt and is limited to basic walls (line/arc)+openings, floors, DirectShape/FreeForm, family forms, grids, views, dimensions; doors/windows via FamilyInstance into openings. Requires ODA Sustaining membership (US$7,500 first year / US$4,500 recurring) plus the BimRv special-module fee; 60-day free trial available. Classified as contingency, and as a Track-D research aid.

Alternatives evaluated and rejected as primary: pyRevit/Dynamo/Revit-MCP (native but need an attended licensed Revit seat -- kept as the interactive debug harness for the same C# core), Speckle (next-gen Revit connector receives as DirectShape; native mapping only in legacy v2), Hypar (converter-based, DirectShape fallback), xBIM/web-ifc/IFC.js (equivalent to path A), gbXML (analytical energy model only, no authoring).

spec/building.schema.json (JSON Schema 2020-12, semver specVersion 0.1.0, additionalProperties:false) makes everything defaultable except intent -- minimal legal spec {"storeys":2,"footprint":[[0,0],[12,0],[12,8],[0,8]]} validates -- with footprint auto-shell + explicit overrides, levels-or-storeys, Revit-style wall constraints (level/topLevel/offsets/unconnected height), line+arc walls, hosted openings by offset/fraction on 'auto-N' or named walls, floors/holes, flat/gable/hip/shed roofs, grids and grid-referenced columns ('1/A'), beams, rooms, a dual-identity type library (open-format layers + revit family/type/rfaPath hints), site/units/project metadata, and a targets block isolating IFC vs Revit back-end knobs.

Recommended architecture: single python spec compiler (validate -> normalize/defaults -> IR with deterministic GUIDs) feeding (Phase 1) an IfcOpenShell writer, (Phase 2) an APS Automation activity running our RvtGen C# add-in that consumes the normalized IR, verified headlessly by a second activity exporting IFC + an element census for CI diff; ODA BimRv only as contingency/research.
